clue.text: Listen ! Listen! Here answer the call of the drum :

definitions.text: answer the call of the drum

indicators.note: 'Here' points to this very spot in the clue, where the letters sit across the two exclamations

explanation.surface: A recruiting sergeant bellows for attention, urging men to march off at the drumbeat.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'Listen!' looks like mere emphasis, but the run straddles the join: listEN LISTen. 'Here' signals that the answer is sitting in the text before you.
explanation.definitionFit: The drum was the traditional call to arms, so responding to it means signing up for military service.

parts.note: the beautiful youth of Greek myth granted eternal sleep, title figure of a long Keats poem

explanation.surface: The fairy-tale princess retold by the Romantic poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sleeping beauty' suggests the fairy-tale princess, but here it is the handsome shepherd whom Selene loved and left in endless slumber; Keats wrote a poem about him.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth the moon goddess loved a shepherd who sleeps for ever, and Keats made him the hero of his 1818 poem.

definitions.note: an adjective in the clue; the answer is a noun for a period of that length

parts.note: an itch is a craving, lust
rum is a spirit, a drink

explanation.surface: A twist on the seven-year itch: a craving for a tipple every half-decade.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on 'the seven-year itch'. A lustrum was the Roman five-yearly purification, hence a five-year period.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Rome a census and purification ceremony was held every five years, giving a word for that span.

parts.note: someone selling writing paper, punningly a person found at a London railway terminus called Victoria

explanation.surface: A Victorian-era newspaper vendor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victorian' suggests the nineteenth century, but Victoria is a London railway station, so a 'station-er' is someone there.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopkeeper selling paper, pens and envelopes; split, the word suggests someone at a railway station.

clue.text: Sound suggestion of glaciers as a marine hazard?

indicators.note: a sound suggestion is something heard, so the spoken phrase for glaciers stands for a different spelling

parts.note: glaciers are slowly moving rivers of ice, i.e. ice flows

explanation.surface: Someone muses on what glaciers might signify for shipping.
explanation.walkthrough: Glaciers are 'ice flows'; said out loud that is identical to the floating slabs that menace ships.
explanation.definitionFit: Floating slabs of sea ice can hole or trap vessels, making them a danger to navigation.

clue.text: Time of low prices back again. That's the ticket

parts.note: a day when goods are sold cheaply
a return is a coming back

explanation.surface: A bargain period has come round once more, and that's just right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's the ticket' looks like a stock phrase of approval but is literal: British Rail sold reduced-fare off-peak round-trip tickets under this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A reduced-fare rail ticket for an off-peak outward and homeward journey on one day.

definitions.meaning: a narrow single-sculling boat used by Eton rowers, who are called wet-bobs

explanation.surface: An odd comedian's joke made for a rower.
explanation.walkthrough: At Eton a wet-bob is a boy who rows; the word also names a narrow sculling boat they used.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means odd and amusing, and also names a slim clinker-built rowing boat.

clue.text: Savoyard, one of the old band

definitions.text: Savoyard, one of the old band

parts.words: Savoyard, one of the old band
parts.note: a member of the Savoy ..., the dance band resident at London's Savoy Hotel in the 1920s

explanation.surface: A Gilbert and Sullivan performer who once played with an old ensemble.
explanation.walkthrough: A Savoyard usually means a Gilbert and Sullivan performer, but here it is a player in the Savoy Hotel's 1920s band, the Savoy Orpheans.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means relating to Orpheus, and the Savoy Hotel's famous dance band took the mythic musician's name.

clue.text: Hail? That's handy for the service

definitions.meaning: a gesture made with the hand in the armed forces

explanation.surface: A greeting that is useful for the military.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handy' means convenient in the surface, but literally 'done with the hand', as the forces' greeting is.
explanation.definitionFit: To greet someone formally, and the raised-hand gesture of respect used in the armed forces.

parts.note: the organ of hearing, misshapen by blows in boxing or rugby

explanation.surface: A radio audience member hurt by a run of industrial walkouts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Listener' suggests a person and 'strikes' industrial action; the listener is an ear and the strikes punches.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeated blows thicken and deform the outer ear, leaving it lumpy like a cabbage-family vegetable.

clue.text: Speak slightingly of the girl's father, with anger

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, so the girl's gives DI'S
pa is an informal word for father
rage is fierce anger

explanation.surface: A young woman's dad, in a temper, runs someone down.
explanation.definitionFit: To belittle or decry something is to talk of it with contempt.

parts.note: Tyneside lies in the North East of England, abbreviated NE
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A Gurkha soldier's homeland is paired with a mate from Newcastle.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyneside is the Newcastle area of north-east England; NE is the standard abbreviation for North East.
explanation.definitionFit: Gurkha soldiers are recruited from the Himalayan kingdom north of India, their native country.

definitions.meaning: the word that goes before 'law' in the phrase for army rule replacing civil government
Marcus Valerius Martialis, the Roman writer of epigrams

explanation.surface: A legal code attributed to a Roman versifier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Law of' reads as one phrase, but 'Law' alone is a clue to the word that precedes it in the phrase for military rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Army rule is called by this name, and the Roman epigrammatist Martialis is known in English by the same word.

parts.note: settlement of a bill eased by a hire-purchase agreement, the 'easy terms' of instalment buying

explanation.surface: A dispute is resolved amicably through mutual consent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settlement' suggests ending a quarrel, but it is settling a debt; 'easy' recalls the phrase 'easy terms' for instalment plans.
explanation.definitionFit: Settling an account means handing over money owed, which is what this word names.

clue.text: The big fellow's an old Turk

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a clothing label for big sizes
a fellow is a man; the 's is the link 'is'

explanation.surface: A large chap is identified as an Ottoman of former times.
explanation.walkthrough: OS (outsize) is a British clothing-size label for extra-large garments.
explanation.definitionFit: The founder of the Ottoman dynasty bore this name, as did several later sultans.

parts.note: flag is another name for the iris plant
a rank is a row, as of soldiers

explanation.surface: A line of garden irises is credited to a naval commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row of irises' reads as a flower bed; flag is the iris, rank the row, and admirals fly their own flags.
explanation.definitionFit: Admirals, vice-admirals and rear-admirals hold the grade entitled to fly a personal flag.

clue.text: Change the order of the back row

parts.note: the rear is the back
a range is a row, as of mountains

explanation.surface: Shuffle the seating at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: To put things in a different sequence is to alter their arrangement.

clue.text: Yet bread may be given away

indicators.note: 'may be' suggests the words Yet bread could take another form once their letters move

explanation.surface: Still, the loaf might be donated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' signals that the letters of YET BREAD are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret given away, or a friend given away, has been disclosed or sold out.

clue.text: Saloon, with seating, open to all

definitions.text: Saloon, with seating, open to all

parts.words: Saloon, with seating, open to all
parts.note: a saloon car whose seats are all reached through their own doors, one for each passenger position

explanation.surface: A bar with chairs welcomes every customer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saloon' suggests a bar room open to the public; it is a saloon car with a door at every seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A car body with entrances to both front and back seats on each side is described by its number of doors.

parts.note: an OB is an old boy, a former pupil of a school
verse is poetry, poems collectively

explanation.surface: A headmaster grades a former pupil's poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: OB (Old Boy) is the British term for a former pupil of a school.
explanation.definitionFit: The side of a coin bearing the monarch's portrait is called its head.

indicators.note: 'perhaps' hints the word crane might be something else once its letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A wading bird spotted on a river in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crane perhaps' suggests a bird as example, but 'perhaps' asks for the letters of CRANE to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: This river in Picardy was the scene of First World War fighting on the Somme front.

definitions.meaning: shut in, as in a small enclosure or a child's bed

explanation.surface: Locked up because of a swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: A crib is a small bed or stall, so to be cribbed is to be confined; to crib is also to copy illicitly.
explanation.definitionFit: Penned in a cramped space, and also having copied someone else's work.

clue.text: Being fast this means being flat out

definitions.text: Being fast this means being flat out

parts.words: Being fast this means being flat out
parts.note: the word that follows fast in the phrase for deep slumber, when someone lies flat

explanation.surface: Going fast means going at top speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' and 'flat out' suggest speed, but 'fast' completes a phrase for deep slumber and 'flat out' means lying down.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone deeply sleeping lies motionless, stretched flat in bed.

clue.text: Where a man could get trimmed in Spain

definitions.text: Where a man could get trimmed in Spain

parts.words: Where a man could get trimmed in Spain
parts.note: an allusion to the opera 'The Barber of ...', set in an Andalusian city

explanation.surface: A traveller looks for a haircut in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: Rossini's opera The Barber of Seville supplies the Spanish city where a man could have his hair cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Rossini's comic opera places its famous barber in this Andalusian city.

parts.note: soothes, calms someone down, as a sedative does

explanation.surface: A sedative does its job.
explanation.definitionFit: To soothe or calm is what a sedative does.

clue.text: The lemur is Jack's? That is right

parts.note: Jack Tar is a sailor, so Jack's gives TAR'S
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the lemur belongs to Jack and is told yes.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Tar is an old nickname for a sailor. The tarsier was once classed with lemurs.
explanation.definitionFit: A small big-eyed primate of South-East Asia, formerly grouped with the lemurs.

clue.text: Flynn may be at fault and look back

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake, be at fault

indicators.note: 'look back' sets the word for look to be read in the opposite direction

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look!

explanation.surface: A film star might make a mistake and then glance over his shoulder.
explanation.definitionFit: The swashbuckling Hollywood actor Flynn had this first name.

parts.note: a lad who makes journeys on others' behalf, who will one day become a man

explanation.surface: Speculation about what tomorrow's skilled craftsman will look like.
explanation.walkthrough: A journeyman is a qualified tradesman, but read literally it is a man who makes journeys; a boy doing that is a future man.
explanation.definitionFit: A lad employed to run messages and deliveries makes trips for others and will grow into a man.

parts.note: a plea is an earnest request
sure means certain

explanation.surface: An appeal bound to bring joy.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name the feeling of happy gratification.

definitions.meaning: bearing a head, as the face of a coin in 19 down does

explanation.surface: Someone won, in the manner of the answer to 19.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 down is the 'head' side of a coin, so something like it bears a head.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead is to go at the front, and a coin face with a portrait is said to have a head on it.
